syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: Units and the International System of Units

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish base units from derived units and express a derived unit in SI base units.
Identify the seven SI base quantities and their units.
Define plane angle and solid angle and state their units, radian and steradian.

topics.title: Significant figures

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the rules to count the significant figures in a reported measurement.
Write a measurement in scientific notation and find its order of magnitude.

topics.title: Arithmetic with significant figures, rounding off and uncertainty

concepts.learning_objective: Report the result of addition, subtraction, multiplication or division with the correct precision.
Round off uncertain digits using the conventions given in the chapter.
Estimate the uncertainty of a result calculated from measured values.

topics.title: Dimensions, dimensional formulae and dimensional equations

concepts.learning_objective: State the dimensions of a physical quantity in terms of the base quantities.
Write and interpret the dimensional formula and dimensional equation of a quantity.

topics.title: Dimensional analysis and its applications

concepts.learning_objective: Use the principle of homogeneity of dimensions to check the consistency of an equation.
Deduce the relation among physical quantities by dimensional analysis.
Explain why a dimensionally consistent equation need not be correct.

topics.title: Describing motion: position, point objects and average velocity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain when a moving body can be treated as a point object and what kinematics studies.
Distinguish average speed from average velocity and compare their magnitudes.

topics.title: Instantaneous velocity and speed

concepts.learning_objective: Find instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocity, v = dx/dt.
Interpret instantaneous velocity as the slope of the tangent to the x-t graph.

topics.title: Acceleration and velocity-time graphs

concepts.learning_objective: Define average and instantaneous acceleration and relate their sign to the chosen axis.
Use the slope and area of a v-t graph to obtain acceleration and displacement.

topics.title: Kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion

concepts.learning_objective: Apply v = v0 + at, x = v0t + at^2/2 and v^2 = v0^2 + 2ax with proper signs.
State the conditions under which the kinematic equations are valid.

topics.title: Applications: free fall, Galileo's law, stopping distance and reaction time

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse vertical motion under gravity, including the top of the path.
Use kinematics to estimate stopping distance and reaction time.

topics.title: Scalars and vectors

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish scalar quantities from vector quantities with examples.
Describe position and displacement vectors and the equality of vectors.

topics.title: Multiplication by real numbers; addition and subtraction of vectors

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the effect of multiplying a vector by a real number.
Add and subtract vectors graphically using the triangle and parallelogram methods and identify the null vector.

topics.title: Resolution of vectors and analytical addition

concepts.learning_objective: Resolve a vector into rectangular components using unit vectors.
Find the magnitude and direction of a resultant analytically, including the law of cosines.

topics.title: Position, velocity and acceleration in a plane

concepts.learning_objective: Define average and instantaneous velocity in a plane and relate velocity to the tangent to the path.
Define average and instantaneous acceleration in a plane in component form.

topics.title: Motion in a plane with constant acceleration

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the vector equations of motion for constant acceleration as two independent one-dimensional motions.

topics.title: Projectile motion

concepts.learning_objective: Show that the path of a projectile is a parabola and analyse its components of motion.
Calculate time of flight, maximum height and horizontal range of a projectile.

topics.title: Uniform circular motion

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and apply the expression for centripetal acceleration in uniform circular motion.
Relate angular speed, time period, frequency and linear speed.

topics.title: Aristotle's fallacy and the law of inertia

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Aristotle's view that a force is needed to keep a body moving uniformly is wrong.
Interpret Galileo's inclined-plane experiments that led to the law of inertia.
Define inertia as the resistance of a body to a change in its state of rest or uniform motion.

topics.title: Newton's first law of motion

concepts.learning_objective: State Newton's first law and relate zero net external force to zero acceleration.
Explain everyday and space situations using Newton's first law.

topics.title: Newton's second law of motion and impulse

concepts.learning_objective: Apply F = dp/dt = ma to calculate forces and accelerations, including apparent weight.
Relate impulse to change in momentum and explain how stretching the impact time reduces force.

topics.title: Newton's third law of motion

concepts.learning_objective: Identify action-reaction pairs and recognise that they act on different bodies.
Calculate the mutual contact force between bodies accelerated together.

topics.title: Conservation of momentum

concepts.learning_objective: State the law of conservation of momentum for an isolated system.
Apply momentum conservation to recoil, explosions and sticking collisions.

topics.title: Equilibrium of a particle

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the condition that the vector sum of concurrent forces is zero for equilibrium.
Resolve forces into components to find unknown tensions in equilibrium.

topics.title: Common forces in mechanics: friction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the self-adjusting nature of static friction and the limiting value mu_s N.
Compare kinetic, static and rolling friction and use the angle of repose.

topics.title: Circular motion and solving problems in mechanics

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the force supplying centripetal force for vehicles on level and banked roads.
Use free-body diagrams to solve connected-body and circular-motion problems.

topics.title: Scalar product and work

concepts.learning_objective: Compute the scalar product of two vectors and use it to find the angle between them.
Calculate the work done by a constant force as W = F.d and interpret its sign.

topics.title: Kinetic energy, work by a variable force and the work-energy theorem

concepts.learning_objective: Relate kinetic energy to mass, speed and linear momentum.
Find the work done by a variable force as the area under the force-displacement graph.
Apply the work-energy theorem: the change in kinetic energy equals the work done by the net force.

topics.title: Potential energy and conservation of mechanical energy

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish conservative and non-conservative forces and relate force to potential energy.
Apply conservation of mechanical energy to falling bodies and a pendulum in a vertical circle.

topics.title: The potential energy of a spring

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the restoring spring force F = -kx for an ideal spring.
Calculate the elastic potential energy (1/2)kx^2 and use it in energy conservation problems.

topics.title: Power

concepts.learning_objective: Define average and instantaneous power and state their units.
Calculate power from P = F.v and relate energy to the kilowatt hour.

topics.title: Collisions

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish elastic and inelastic collisions by what is conserved.
Find final velocities and kinetic energy loss in one-dimensional collisions.
Analyse an elastic collision in two dimensions using momentum and energy conservation.

chapters.title: Systems of Particles and Rotational Motion

topics.title: Rigid bodies and the centre of mass

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish pure translation from rotation and identify the motion possible for a rigid body fixed along a line.
Locate the centre of mass of a system of particles and of symmetric bodies.

topics.title: Motion of the centre of mass and linear momentum of a system

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the centre of mass moves as if all mass were concentrated there and all external forces acted on it.
Relate the total linear momentum of a system to its mass and the velocity of its centre of mass.

topics.title: Vector product of two vectors

concepts.learning_objective: State the magnitude, direction and properties of the vector product.
Evaluate vector products using unit vectors and use them to find areas.

topics.title: Angular velocity, torque and angular momentum

concepts.learning_objective: Use v = omega x r to relate linear and angular velocity.
Calculate torque as the moment of a force, r x F.
Define the angular momentum of a particle and relate its rate of change to torque.

topics.title: Equilibrium of a rigid body

concepts.learning_objective: State the conditions for translational and rotational equilibrium and the effect of a couple.
Apply the principle of moments to levers and balanced rods.
Explain when the centre of gravity coincides with the centre of mass.

topics.title: Moment of inertia

concepts.learning_objective: Define moment of inertia and identify the factors on which it depends.
Define and calculate the radius of gyration of a body.

topics.title: Kinematics and dynamics of rotational motion about a fixed axis

concepts.learning_objective: Use the equations of uniformly accelerated rotational motion.
Apply tau = I alpha to bodies rotating about a fixed axis.
Calculate work and power in rotational motion.

topics.title: Angular momentum for rotation about a fixed axis

concepts.learning_objective: Apply conservation of angular momentum, I omega = constant, when external torque is zero.

topics.title: Kepler's laws of planetary motion

concepts.learning_objective: State Kepler's law of orbits and locate the Sun relative to a planet's elliptical orbit.
Relate Kepler's law of areas to conservation of angular momentum under a central force.
Use T^2 proportional to a^3 to compare the periods of planets or satellites.

topics.title: Universal law of gravitation and the gravitational constant

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Newton's law F = G m1 m2 / r^2 to find the force between two masses.
State the force exerted by a uniform spherical shell on a point mass outside and inside it.
Describe how G was measured by Cavendish and state its value and SI unit.

topics.title: Acceleration due to gravity of the earth

concepts.learning_objective: Express g at the earth's surface as G M_E / R_E^2 and use it to compare g on different bodies.
Use g, R_E and G to determine the mass of the earth.

topics.title: Acceleration due to gravity below and above the surface

concepts.learning_objective: Find the variation of g with height above the earth's surface, exactly and for h much less than R_E.
Find the variation of g with depth below the earth's surface using g(d) = g(1 - d/R_E).

topics.title: Gravitational potential energy

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of a system of masses with zero at infinity.
Define gravitational potential as potential energy per unit mass.
Explain mgh as an approximation to the change in gravitational potential energy for small heights.

topics.title: Escape speed

concepts.learning_objective: Derive and use the escape speed v_e = sqrt(2 g R_E) = sqrt(2 G M_E / R_E).
Apply energy conservation to bodies launched at or above escape speed and explain why the moon has no atmosphere.

topics.title: Earth satellites and their energy

concepts.learning_objective: Find the orbital speed and period of a satellite in a circular orbit around the earth.
Find the kinetic, potential and total energy of an orbiting satellite and explain weightlessness.
